topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I called my childhood best friend today, the one I used to spend every summer with, building forts and chasing fireflies. When I mentioned those times, there was a long pause on the line. "I'm sorry," they said, their voice breaking a little, "I don’t remember those specifics. It’s been so long, and..." Their voice trailed off, and I could hear them take a deep breath. I felt the words stick in my throat as I searched for something, anything, to say. We eventually talked about other things, the current, the safe, but the conversation didn't last long. As we said goodbye, I couldn’t help but replay every word, every pause, trying to piece together what was left of our shared past.
